<description>
**Problem:** `PrecomputedTransactionData` could be default-constructed and filled later with `Init()`.
That allowed an object to exist without transaction-specific data and left a public reuse path that was easy to get wrong.
The old `Init()` guard only checked [`m_spent_outputs_ready`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/2063f02bd5edebe1b5c9635db8850220811ebc90/src/script/interpreter.cpp#L1415), which remained false after initialization without spent outputs even when the BIP143 prevout, sequence, and output hashes were already cached.
No current caller reuses an object across transactions, so validation and signing results are unchanged.
`btck_script_pubkey_verify()` in the experimental kernel C API also copied caller-supplied txdata on each verification call.

**Fix:** Remove default construction and `Init()` so each `PrecomputedTransactionData` object is built for one transaction.
Callers that already have the transaction and optional spent outputs construct it directly.
Validation stores txdata in `std::optional` and emplaces it only after a script-cache miss, keeping precomputation lazy.
`ConnectBlock()` also leaves txdata storage empty when assumevalid skips script checks, covering #35663.
The kernel verification path binds directly to caller-supplied txdata and constructs a local fallback only when needed.
</description>

[2026-07-09] rc:3548130049 inline on src/script/interpreter.cpp by l0rinc (member):
I agree that resetting readiness flags inside `Init()` still leaves a reuse API around and makes the type responsible for defending against misuse after construction (I was hoping someone would object).

I’ll rework this so that `PrecomputedTransactionData` is always built for one transaction and has no public reinitialization path:
* Call sites that already have the transaction and spent outputs can construct it directly.
* Call sites that need to wait, such as validation before the script execution cache check, can store `std::optional<PrecomputedTransactionData>` and `emplace()` once all required data has been gathered.

This also seems like a natural place to fold in #35663: validation already needs optional txdata storage, so the assumevalid path can leave the per-block txdata vector empty when script checks are skipped, while still resizing it before any queued checks can take pointers into it.

tACK 35a8964f884391cf8aa2434c379561693b21f1f2

On which staleness this prevents: on the base (7988380da9), `Init(A, {})` for a transaction with a witness, then `Init(B, spent_outputs)` for one without, passes the old `assert(!m_spent_outputs_ready)`, since A was given no spent outputs. The object keeps A's BIP143 hashes, so B's BIP143 sighash comes out different from a fresh object's. I found no caller that initializes twice, so this is not reachable today; with this PR such code no longer compiles.

I compared 5961 BIP143 and BIP341 key path sighashes from a library I maintain with `SignatureHash` and `SignatureHashSchnorr`, on base and head, with txdata built with and without spent outputs and with and without `force`. All agree, and Taproot without spent outputs is refused on both. On head the unit tests pass (155 ctest entries, `script_assets_tests` skipped for lack of data), and so does `test_kernel`.

The kernel commit stops `btck_script_pubkey_verify` from copying the caller's txdata on every call. I measured base against head with a static Release libbitcoinkernel on an Apple M5, verifying a trivial script with precomputed txdata for a 10000-input transaction. One call takes about 100 µs on base and 0.17 µs on head, and the base cost grows with the input count. Verifying all 10000 inputs once drops from about 1 s to under 2 ms. I can share the harnesses in a gist.
</statements>
